problems: All four dossiers validate with 0 errors. maratha-empire carries 2 slug warnings (kolhapur-state, janjira-state have no dossier yet) and 1 gazetteer warning (Karwar).

Cliopatria 'Maratha Empire' 1820-1845 shapes (82,885 km2 around Gwalior) are marked wrong: the Maratha Empire ended in June 1818; the cells belong to Gwalior (Shinde), whose dossier must be written by another batch.

Cliopatria 'Carnatic Sultanate' 1800-1802 shape includes the whole Thanjavur kingdom (48 cells), which passed to the Company in 1799; corrected in carnatic-sultanate_1800. The Carnatic dossier starts in 1710 (not 1713) and ends 26 July 1801 (not 1802).

Cliopatria 'Sikhs' 1709-1717 is one Sirhind polygon repeated for nine years; it is valid only May-December 1710 (Banda Singh Bahadur's state, typed rebel). The mughal-empire dossier has no contest or recovery event for Banda's rising; add one.
Maratha Empire 1677-1690 shapes are only the Kolhapur/south Konkan/Karwar patch, and 1691-1717 has no shape; bridged with new keyframes at confidence 1.

Page counts: Maratha Empire 9 pages, Thanjavur 3 new (plus the Shivaji page reused), Sikhs 2 (one was the 'Battle of Lohgarh' disambiguation page), Carnatic 5; 19 distinct pages opened in total, 23 source entries across the four dossiers (some pages are cited by two dossiers).
WebFetch returns a model summary of each page, not raw text; quotes in notes are the phrases the tool returned in quotation marks, other statements are close paraphrases.

The mughal-empire and portuguese-empire dossiers (other groups) already record counterpart events for the Marathas (Jinji 1698, Satara 1700, Malwa 1738, Nagar Haveli 1783): the 1783 Nagar Haveli loss has no matching event in maratha-empire because that page was not opened here.

Hyderabad State, Kingdom of Mysore, Nawabs of Bengal, Nawab of Awadh and Nayaks of Madurai dossiers (other sa-05 parts, not yet written at the time) are used as counterpart slugs in gain/loss/contest events (udgir/Khargone/Handia, Maratha-Mysore wars, Orissa, Madurai 1736).
